title: Word Parts as Clues
keyIdea: A new word is often a word you know with a small part added. Find the root word first, then read each extra part as a clue to the meaning. -ed at the end says it already happened (kicked). un- at the front says not (unkind) or undo (untie). -s at the end of a thing word says more than one (cups), unless the s is part of the root, as in bus. -er has two jobs: on a doing word it names the person who does it (a painter paints), and on a describing word it means more (taller).
familyTip: When you meet a long word in a book, cover the front or the end with your finger and ask what word is left. Then ask what the hidden part adds. Try unpacked: cover un and ed to find pack, then talk about what un and ed tell you. Swap jobs too: you say a clue (a person who bakes), your child says the word.

visual.caption: What does the er mean? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort -ed words by time, read un- words, match -s words to one or many, sort the two jobs of -er, then build words from a clue.

kid: A long word can be a word you know with a small part stuck on. The word you know is the root. Find the root first. Then look at the parts at the front and the end. Each part is a clue.

ed at the end means it already happened. Sam kicked the ball. That is over. He is not kicking it now. un at the front can mean not. unkind means not kind. It can also undo a job. untie means take the knot out.
s at the end of a thing word means more than one. cups is more than one cup. Be careful: bus just ends in s. There is only one bus.
er does two jobs. A painter is a person who paints. Taller means more tall. Look at the root to tell which one it is.
adult: Ages 5 to 8. This is using morphology for meaning: the US Common Core asks children to use frequently occurring inflections and affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word (L.K.4b, L.1.4b and c), and to use a known root to work out a new word with a prefix (L.2.4b and c). In England the same endings (-s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est) and the prefix un- are taught in Year 1 spelling and word reading, with -er and -est on describing words.

The terms: a morpheme is the smallest part of a word with meaning. The root (or base word) carries the main meaning; a prefix such as un- goes before it and a suffix such as -ed goes after it. Inflections like -s and -ed change number or tense but not the kind of word. Agentive -er (painter, teacher) makes a noun from a verb, while comparative -er (taller, softer) is added to an adjective, which is why the root decides the meaning.

Common mistakes: reading un- as very or again (unhappy as very happy, unlock as lock it again), thinking any word that ends in s means more than one (bus, dress), treating every -er as more (a farmer as more farm), and missing the -ed ending when reading aloud, so the time clue is lost. The other slip is guessing from the first letters instead of finding the whole root first.

In the lab your child sorts eight words into happens now or already happened, picks the meaning of five un- words, taps one or many pictures for six words (including bus and dress), sorts eight -er words into a person or more, and then builds five words from a meaning clue by dragging un to the front or -ed, -s or -er to the end of a root.

practice.prompt: Mia painted a picture. When did she paint it?
practice.hint: Look at the end of painted. What does ed tell you?
practice.explain: painted ends in ed, and ed means it already happened. The painting is done.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters. You put un at the front and change nothing else. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: un has two letters. The root stays the same.
practice.explain: The root keeps its {n} letters and un adds 2, so the new word has {=n+2} letters. kind has 4 letters and unkind has 6.

practice.hint: un at the front of a describing word flips it.
practice.explain: un in front of safe means not, so unsafe means not safe. un never means very or again.

practice.prompt: A list has {a} words that end in ed, like jumped, and {b} words with no ending, like jump. How many words tell you it already happened?
practice.hint: Only the ed ending is the clue for already happened.
practice.explain: Only the {a} words with ed say it already happened. The {b} words with no ending do not.

practice.hint: You can farm. er on a doing word names a person.
practice.explain: farm is a doing word here: you can farm. A farmer is the person who farms. er means more only on a describing word, like taller.

pool.prompt: Which word tells you there is more than one?
pool.hint: Look for an s that was added to the root.
pool.explain: hats is hat with s added, so there is more than one. In bus the s is part of the word, so there is one bus.

pool.prompt: Ben unpacked his bag. What did he do?
choices: He took things out of it
pool.hint: Find the root pack. What do un and ed add?
pool.explain: un undoes pack, so things came out, and ed says it already happened.

pool.hint: fast is a describing word. Which ending means more?
pool.explain: er on a describing word means more, so faster means more fast. un means not, and s does not mean more fast.

pool.prompt: What is the root word in unlocked?
pool.hint: Take off the part at the front and the part at the end.
pool.explain: Take off un and ed and lock is left. lock is the root; un and ed are the clues.

pool.hint: Can you sing? Then er names a person.
pool.explain: sing is a doing word, so a singer is a person who sings.
un means not here, so unwell means not well, or ill.

pool.prompt: A root word has {n} letters. You add ed to the end and the root does not change, like jump and jumped. How many letters now?
pool.hint: ed has two letters. Keep every letter of the root.
pool.explain: {n} letters in the root plus 2 for ed makes {=n+2}. jump has 4 letters and jumped has 6.

pool.prompt: You read {a} words. {b} of them start with un. How many do not start with un?
pool.hint: Take away the un words from all the words.
pool.explain: {a} words take away the {b} un words leaves {=a-b} without un.

pool.prompt: Grace is a fast runner. What does runner tell you?
choices: Grace is a person who runs
pool.hint: run is a doing word. What does er add to a doing word?
pool.explain: runner is a person who runs. er on a doing word names the person.
